haiku-low.q1: It creates a short-lived pending login (row plus p2f cookie) and redirects to the code page. No session is created.
haiku-low.q2: Only after the first valid code confirms setup, when pending_secret moves into secret. Sign-in ignores the pending secret before that.
haiku-low.q3: An unused matching code is deleted, the pending login ends, and a session starts. The notification email is queued and does not affect sign-in. It reports the remaining code count.
haiku-low.q4: Five wrong entries, or five minutes passing (noticed when the code page is opened or posted). The user goes to the password page.
haiku-low.q5: Every other session of the user is deleted. Only the current session is kept.
haiku-low.q6: No. last_used_step only accepts later steps, blocking replay. Drift tolerance is the current 30-second step plus one step before and one after.
haiku-low.q7: In one transaction: pending_secret moves to secret, last_used_step is set, old recovery codes are replaced with 10 new hashed codes. First setup also deletes other sessions. If it fails, it rolls back and no codes are shown.
haiku-low.q8: In the pending_logins table, keyed by the hash of the p2f cookie's raw token. Removed on success, after 5 wrong entries, on expiry when seen, on a new password login, or on turning 2FA off.
haiku-low.q9: user_totp holds secret, pending_secret and last_used_step. recovery_codes holds hashes. 2FA is on when user_totp.secret is non-empty.
haiku-low.q10: Sign-in keeps using the active secret, so the old app still works. If abandoned, the pending secret stays until the user starts again or turns 2FA off.
haiku-low.q11: A 6-digit value is treated as an app code, anything else as a recovery code. Wrong or used recovery codes count as wrong entries toward the limit of five.

sonnet.q1: Not a session. A correct password with an active secret creates a short-lived pending login (row in pending_logins, 5 min, p2f cookie) and redirects to the code page. No sid cookie is set until an app code or unused recovery code is entered.
sonnet.q2: Once the first valid code is confirmed during setup, the pending secret moves into secret (the active secret), which sign-in checks. While Setup is pending, sign-in ignores it and signs in with just a password.
sonnet.q3: The server hashes the value, finds an unused hash for the user, deletes that code and the pending row, clears p2f, calls start_session() (Signed in) and calls enqueue_email() saying a recovery code was used and how many remain (9 after first use). Sign-in does not depend on the email: it is queued and retried, and never blocks or fails the request. last_used_step is not changed.
sonnet.q4: 5 wrong entries, or 5 minutes passing (expiry noticed only when the code page is next opened or posted). The pending row is deleted, p2f cleared, and the user is sent to the password page.
sonnet.q5: On first confirmation (turn on), in the same transaction, every other session of the user is deleted. Only the current session (the one whose sid cookie hashes to a sessions.token_hash) is kept.
sonnet.q6: No. A code is accepted only if its time step is later than last_used_step, which is set on acceptance, so replay is blocked. Drift tolerance is the current 30-second time step plus one before and one after.
sonnet.q7: In one transaction: pending_secret moves into secret; last_used_step is set to the accepted/confirming step; old recovery codes are deleted and 10 new hashed ones inserted. First confirmation also deletes all other sessions; replacement does not. If it fails, it rolls back: nothing changes, the user sees an error, no codes are shown. On first setup the pending secret is kept so the user can retry. On replacement the old authenticator still works.
sonnet.q8: Stored in the pending_logins table (token_hash, user_id, expires_at = now + 5 min, wrong_count; at most one row per user). The browser holds the raw random token in the p2f cookie (httponly, secure, samesite Lax, 5-minute max age), and the server finds the row by hashing the cookie. It is removed by a successful sign-in (app or recovery code), 5 wrong entries, expiry noticed on the code page, a new password sign-in for the same user (deletes existing row), or turning 2FA off. Bulk deletion of expired rows is not decided.
sonnet.q9: user_totp (one row per user) holds secret (sealed active secret), pending_secret (sealed, for setup or replacement) and last_used_step (replay protection, per user). recovery_codes holds user_id and code_hash per code. 2FA is on when an active secret exists (secret non-empty); it is off when secret is empty.
sonnet.q10: The new secret sits in pending_secret and sign-in ignores it. Sign-in still uses the old active secret, so the old app keeps working. If the user abandons it, the old app still works and the pending secret stays until the user starts again or turns 2FA off.
sonnet.q11: By format: a 6-digit value is an app code (step 10). Any other value is treated as a recovery code (step 11), because recovery codes are never 6 digits. Yes, an unknown or used recovery code is a wrong entry and adds 1 to wrong_count, with a limit of 5.
sonnet.q12: Not designed. Product has not decided whether support may reset 2FA or how identity would be checked (open question). The document gives no path.
